Write it to .agent-work/cleanup-b-context-identity/MISSION_FRAME.md — that exact path is what the c6 gate reads, so a frame parked anywhere else reads as no frame at all. For a trivial local/mechanical change where the map adds nothing, shrink or skip the frame and say so in its intent; c6 is waivable, so take that escape as a RECORDED waiver (<engine> waive plan --cond c6 --authority human --reason '...') rather than as a silent skip. The c6 gate runs map_orient.py verify-frame over that file: every anchor id the frame cites must exist in the map inventory the context step resolved, or — when context came back DEGRADED — must be one of the substitutes the receipt hash-pinned there, so the frame is compared against a committed prior declaration instead of a same-breath assertion. Measured against this epic's baseline five runs it has sensitivity 0/4 and specificity 0/1, and it inherits the late-anchor defect it was built next to, because anchors-in-a-late-frame is compliance without sequence. The load-bearing map-first anchor is at the context step ('before you open any source file'), which is why verify-orientation is gated there and verify-frame is gated only here. Do NOT 'fix' that asymmetry by also running verify-frame at context: no frame exists at context — the step runs before understand and plan — and the only way to make it pass there is to let an ABSENT frame pass, which is exactly the refusal the whole check is built on. If verify-frame ever has to be context-safe, give it a step-scoped mode; never a vacuous pass. For any low-confidence/stale/disputed map area the run depends on, alter the plan accordingly: add a scout/verification gate or surface it to the human as a decision — never author gates that silently trust an unverified map. Before the plan-approved checkpoint run plan-alternatives (parallel gate-plan candidates under distinct constraints, via the references/design-it-twice-brief.md contract) and a cold plan critic (reads the candidate plan + mission frame only, no authoring context); both bias-to-yes — any skip is surfaced as a named untaken road — and the panel-vs-single choice is surfaced to the human at plan approval. execute.context_headroom_note: #467. Absolute-token context reserve for THIS gate only: the engine subtracts it from both the soft and hard caps before dividing by the model's window, so `execute` may not be BEGUN with less than this much room left below the hard cap. It makes the imperative's existing prose instruction ('ensure context headroom before entering') enforceable, and it can only ever tighten -- no gate can raise a threshold. WHY 30000, and it is a GUESS, revisable in place: `execute` is the run's longest gate and the one that cannot be abandoned halfway, because it drives every crew gate and each crew dispatch costs tens of thousands of tokens. The only observation available was a commander sitting at ~127K fill after a cold resume plus one full three-task gate -- which bounds one gate's marginal cost in the tens of thousands but cannot separate it from the resume baseline. 30K is a round number at the low end of that range: on claude-opus-5 (1M window, 80K soft / 150K hard) it moves execute's begin-work line from 15% to 12% and its advisory from 8% to 5%, while every other gate keeps the shipped default. The named settle experiment (read fill_fraction across completed commander runs at the moment execute was started) is NOT runnable from existing artifacts -- gauge.json keeps only the latest reading and the per-gate context manifests record no fill -- so a later run may revise this number here, in this one place, without re-deriving anything.

None of the old is-.agent-work-gitignored reasoning applies to it. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): by default call the spine_lease MCP tool with action=release (this is your own spine; the door needs no session id argument). CLI fallback: <engine> release --session-id commander-cleanup-b-context-identity. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

the work is REACHABLE: this branch has a pull request that is OPEN or MERGED. A merged PR is reachable work; a closed-unmerged one is not, and neither is no PR at all. A terminal spine and a pushed branch describe the run, not the ref -- CI never runs on an unopened branch, and every commander that reached a terminal spine without opening one had to be chased for it. Open the PR even if the work is unfinished; declare FINAL or PENDING in its title and hand the merge up. Two properties of the check text are load-bearing. The branch is derived at CHECK time from the repo root, never resolved at instantiation: init instantiates the spine before it starts the branch, so the branch need not exist yet -- and a literal branch placeholder is not a resolver-owned token, so instantiation cannot catch one and would ship it unsubstituted. The count is compared in the SHELL because the engine's verdict for a command condition is the EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded: gh --jq 'length > 0' prints true or false but exits 0 either way, so that form can never fail.
